title: We Manufacture Our Own Masters · Why read this book?

narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.description: An articulate adult English narrator with warm authority and a thoughtful, varied cadence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Confiscate every fortune, and someone still decides who gets a home and who may leave.

direction.delivery: Quiet and concrete, let the second clause land.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: We Manufacture Our Own Masters calls these traps antinomies, and finds them in every camp.

direction.delivery: State the title plainly; stress every camp.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The author knew them from communism, where levelled incomes still hid a nobility without titles.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its test is adversarial: judge each system by what a hostile leader could do.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then ask how the people affected could stop that leader.

direction.delivery: Brief pause before stop, then direct.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Liberalism, Chinese order, private cities and guaranteed income all face the same scrutiny.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Appendices separate supported claims from hypothesis, and the book turns its test on itself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Markets can let winners close entry, and floods of noise can silence speech without censors.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Artificial intelligence may cheapen expertise while handing power to whoever owns the infrastructure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A free order, the book argues, is measured by what citizens can refuse without starving.

direction.delivery: Slow down; land refuse without starving.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with chapter one, Antinomies Are Not Accidents, and run its test on your favourite system.

direction.delivery: Open and warm, a direct invitation.
